## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kuladūsaka* (“Being a corrupter of families”) is the thirteenth rule of the *Saṅghādisesa* section in the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. The text concerns a monastic who corrupts lay families, causing local householders to lose faith in the Buddha's teachings [SuttaCentral]. According to the origin narrative, the rule was instituted following the corrupt conduct of the group of six monks (*chabbaggiya*), a faction responsible for offenses prompting many Vinaya rules [SuttaCentral]. Monks guilty of corrupting families are subject to formal banishment from the locality; persistent resistance to banishment after repeated formal admonitions incurs a *saṅghādisesa* offense, entailing suspension [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Cross-tradition parallels to this rule are preserved widely across early Buddhist monastic codes [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral identifies direct rule parallels in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Ss 13) and *Bhikkhu Parivāra* (Ss 13), counterpart rules for nuns in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Ss 17), and corresponding *Saṅghādisesa* rules in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Dharmaguptaka recensions extant in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes canonical passage-level parallels in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10.44, *Kusinārasutta*) and the Khandhaka chapters Kd 11 (*Kammakkhandhaka*), Kd 15 (*Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka*), and Kd 19 (*Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhaka*), with mentions in *Parivāra* 17, *Cūḷaniddesa* 23, and *Mahāniddesa* 14 [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus corroborates these alignments, revealing extensive Pali-internal sharing with Kd 11 (particularly §1.4.8–1.7.15 matching Kd 11 §13.4.21–13.7.19), Kd 15, the Pātimokkha codes, and related Vibhaṅga rules, as well as machine matches with Sanskrit and Tibetan Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga literature [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
